3. Defendant Nos. 1, 2-7 and 9 contested the suit by filing two separate written statements denying all the material allegations made in the plaint, contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and manner as the suit is barred by law of limitation and all the suit properties were not brought into the hotchpotch. The suit is also bad for defect of the parties and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 "Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the petitioner took us through the impugned judgment and papers on record, and submitted that by the admitted declaration or Shoronlipi dated 13-12-2004 the suit land in question has been partitioned amicably by allotting specific saham and specific area, therefore, in case of inclusion of any other land in hotchpotch or schedule of the plaint, the area of the saham as already allotted by mutual agreement or consent would have not been changed in any way." 

 8. Mr Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing for respondent Nos. l (f-h) made submissions in support of the impugned judgement and order of the High Court Division. He adds that in this partition suit, there is defect of hotchpot since all the properties left by Hakim Bashirul Haque Chowdhury has not been brought in the schedule of the plaint and, as such, the defendant-respondent are being seriously prejudiced. He also adds that this case is also bad for defect of parties. He finally submits that since the property in dispute has already been partitioned through a registered deed of declaration and, as such, there is no necessity to file this partition suit in the Court. 

 12. One the other hand, the contesting defendant denied the aforesaid allegation of the plaintiff (petitioner) and counter claimed that as per paras 6 and 7 of the declaration all the properties of the parties have not been included in the schedule of the plaint and, as such, the suit is bad for defect of hotchpotch and thus, the suit is not maintainable which is liable to be dismissed. Defendant Nos. 2-7/9 contended that the suit is bad for defect of parties. It has been further alleged that after the death of Hakim Bashirul Haque Chowdhury, his heirs decided to make partition of the suit land and accordingly, on 13-12-2004 executed a declaration in respect of the suit land and building standing thereon in which the respective share of the parties has been allocated and it was also decided that the cosharers would effect partition of the suit land as per the declaration within 1 year from its execution. But unfortunately, defendant No.1 did not comply with the terms and conditions of the declaration. 

 14. From which it appears that the suit land and the building standing thereon have been divided into several parts and those have been allocated among the co-sharers of the property appended in the schedule of the plaint. PW 1, DWs 1 and 2 are the heirs of Hakini Bashirul Haque Chowdhury who have admitted in their deposition and cross-examination that the said deed of declaration was being executed and registered among them. They have also conceded that they have no objection if the suit land and building standing thereon would be partitioned on basis of deed of declaration. The other defendants, i.e. defendant Nos.2-7/9 agreed to effect partition according to the claim of the plaintiff and they have claimed separate saham in respect of their legitimate' portion of property. The only objection raised by the defendant is that all the properties of the deceased Bashirul Haque Chowdhury have not been brought into the hotchpotch and, as such, the suit is not maintainable in its present from. In this regard, the trial Court decided that though all the properties of the deceased 13shirul Haque Chowdhury have not been brought into hotchpotch, the suit land and the building standing thereon can be made partitioned separately among the co-sharers on the basis of the deed of declaration dated 13-12-2004 since the same has been executed by them on the basis of mutual understanding and considering the convenience and inconvenience among them. Having considered the claim and counter-claim of the parties, we are to ascertain as to whether the partial partition is possible only for the suit land as has been decided by the learned Judge of the trial Court. It appears that respondent No.1 alone is in the possession of the suit property and with a view to maintain and prolongation of his possession in the suit property, he denied partition as per their admitted declaration or shoronlipi.
